question: Should `socket.drain` preserve the existing Gateway slow-consumer drop behavior, or intentionally close slow subscribed clients during teardown?
rationale: This is a Gateway protocol/backpressure contract choice with compatibility and availability impact; code review can recommend the conservative default, but maintainers own any deliberate client-disconnect semantics.

options.title: Preserve existing slow-consumer behavior
options.body: Keep teardown broadcasts from disconnecting slow clients by matching the existing `sessions.changed` backpressure policy, then document the event.

options.title: Approve disconnect-on-drain
options.body: Allow `socket.drain` to close slow clients, but require explicit docs, tests, and release-note context because this changes the websocket contract.

options.title: Defer the new event
options.body: Do not merge the public `socket.drain` surface until the Gateway lifecycle event model is designed more broadly.

recommendation.title: Preserve existing slow-consumer behavior
recommendation.body: Keep teardown broadcasts from disconnecting slow clients by matching the existing `sessions.changed` backpressure policy, then document the event.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest recent history across Gateway session and broadcaster refactors in the available local history.
